standard_prerequisites.name: The abstract lifting lemma for complexes with respect to a class of modules closed under the five listed properties
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the complex P^bullet of finite stably free modules.

standard_prerequisites.name: The class of finite stably free modules is an exact category, and finite stably free modules lift over an ideal consisting of elements of 1 + I
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies properties (2) and (4) of the lifting lemma.

core_obligations: Apply the abstract lifting lemma for complexes using the class P of all finite stably free R-modules (proof lines 19532-19534).
Check property (1) as immediate, and property (2) via the exact category statement for stably free modules (proof lines 19534-19535).
Check property (3) via Nakayama's lemma, quoting the Algebra statement (proof lines 19536-19537).
Check property (4) via the liftability of finite stably free R/I-modules to finite stably free R-modules (proof lines 19538-19540).
Check part (5) because a pseudo-coherent complex is represented by a bounded above complex of finite free R-modules (proof lines 19541-19542).
Conclude that the lifting lemma gives P^bullet, and that the final freeness assertion follows from the statement on isomorphism classes of finite projective lifts (proof lines 19543-19544).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an ideal I, a complex E^bullet of R/I-modules and an object K of D(R), under four hypotheses: E^bullet is a bounded above complex of finite stably free R/I-modules; K tensor^L_R R/I is represented by E^bullet in D(R/I); K^bullet is pseudo-coherent; and every element of 1 + I is invertible. It concludes that there is a bounded above complex P^bullet of finite stably free R-modules representing K in D(R) with P^bullet tensor_R R/I isomorphic to E^bullet, and moreover that P^i is free wherever E^i is (source lines 19516-19530). The proof is structurally parallel to the projective case: it applies the abstract lifting lemma for complexes with respect to the class of all finite stably free R-modules (proof lines 19532-19534). Property (1) is immediate; property (2) follows from the exact category statement for stably free modules; property (3) follows from Nakayama's lemma; property (4) follows from the liftability of finite stably free modules along an ideal consisting of elements of 1 + I; and part (5) holds because a pseudo-coherent complex is represented by a bounded above complex of finite free modules (proof lines 19534-19542). The final assertion follows from the statement on isomorphism classes of finite projective lifts (proof lines 19543-19544). The non-routine content is the verification of the eigenvalue-type hypothesis, namely that the stably free class is well behaved under the given condition on 1 + I, which is what makes property (2) and property (4) available.
